docs.title: lantern
docs.body:
# lantern

A personal record that can answer questions about itself.

The premise is that an archive and a record are different objects. An archive keeps; a record carries the shape of its own accumulation, so it can be asked when something arrived, what it arrived from, and whether anyone has looked at it since.

docs.title: ADR-0001 — One store, divided by who may write
docs.body:
# ADR-0001 — One store, divided by who may write

Status: accepted

Dividing a personal store by what the data is produces categories that stop being true within a year. Dividing it by who may write produces three that have held: what the world recorded about you, what you wrote, and what a machine concluded. The third may never be an input to itself, which is what makes the whole thing rebuildable.

docs.title: tidewrack
docs.body:
# tidewrack

Near-duplicate detection for prose, tuned for short passages.

Filing is not containment. The same paragraph turns up under a second name often enough that any system deciding what to publish by folder alone will eventually publish the thing it meant to withhold.

docs.title: CONTEXT
docs.body:
# CONTEXT

Vocabulary for the publication step.

**serve** — a remote reader may see it. **hold** — it never leaves. There is no third state and no default: an undeclared thing fails the build rather than guessing, so nothing is published by being forgotten.

docs.title: ostrander
docs.body:
# ostrander

A two-pass reading log. Shelved until I know what I want from it.

The first pass builds a map and is not allowed to argue. The second pass is where the disagreements go. The software never captured that distinction, which is why it is here and not in use.
